title: Environmental stress and psychosomatic diseases: The therapeutic potential of a Kneipp health resort
summary:
Depression is one of the most common mental health disorders. In addition to biological and social factors, environmental stressors such as noise, air pollution, or workplace stress can also affect mental health. However, little is currently known about whether such environmental stressors also influence the success of inpatient psychosomatic rehabilitation focused on Kneipp therapies.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether people exposed to varying levels of environmental stressors benefit to different degrees from a six-week inpatient psychosomatic therapy program incorporating Kneipp therapies.

The study includes adults with moderate depression who are being treated at the Das Alpreflect clinic in Hopfen am See (a Kneipp spa in Bavaria). Before, during, and 3, 6, and 9 months after therapy, participants complete several questionnaires regarding their mental health, quality of life, and environmental stress. During their hospital stay, nasal secretion and urine samples are also collected. These are analyzed for biological markers associated with depression and stress responses. A subgroup also wears a smartwatch to track heart rate, heart rate variability, and sleep.

The results are intended to help better understand the influence of environmental stress on the success of depression treatment and to tailor future psychosomatic treatments more specifically to patients’ needs.
conditions: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate

interventions.name:
This is a single-arm observational study. All participants receive the same treatment: multimodal inpatient psychotherapy, including Kneipp therapies. There is no randomized intervention or control arm.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adults (aged 18–65) who are spending a 6-week therapeutic stay at the Alpreflect clinic in Hopfen am See
− Existing diagnosis of (1) recurrent depressive disorder, currently in a moderate episode, or (2) a first-time, moderate depressive episode
− Ability to understand the study information and provide written consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
− medical contraindications for Kneipp treatments (e.g. severe cardiovascular diseases)
− insufficient language skills that make communication and informed consent impossible
− that make communication impossible
− lack of email access (access is required to take part in online surveys)
